messages.body_plain:
Hi Anjo,
This concerns function g.readaccfile <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/b6a985751120d1ef62d6f25fb992a31129f88f6c/R/g.readaccfile.R>. I think we did make this function work for one decimal separator without trying to test whether it works for other decimal separator settings.
Can you create a GitHub issue https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues with an example file for us to test? If needed a shortened one  with only the first couple of hundred lines is fine.
Thanks, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] sleep detection of the first night
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] sleep detection of the first night
messages.body_plain:
Part 5 does this to extract the waking up time from the first incomplete night. So, if you are interested in the waking-up time then it should be reported in the part5 output.
For part4 I intentionally did not implement this because I did not expect value of it for sleep research. How would you report sleep duration if you know the measurement does not cover the entire night?

What you could do to trick the code is to use dayborder = 1, in that way it will use 1am as midnight and will give you an estimate for the first night..I suppose you could to the same for the last night by changing dayborder to -1. I have never tried this myself, so if it does not work then I am afraid I cannot help you further.
Vincent

On Tue, 27 Nov 2018 at 22:45, Johannes Jaunig <johanne...@uni-graz.at> wrote:

> Dear Vincent!
> Dear Group Members!
>
> We would like to estimate sleeping time. The sleep algorithm works fine for all days except for the first night (starting with Sunday midnight). We had 7 days of measuring from Monday (00:01) to Sunday (23:59). Does anybody know a way to estimate sleep also for the first night although there is no interval "overstretching two days"? Since it should be similar to nights when participants went to bed after midnight...
> We do not have a sleep log and used the following parameters in part 4:
>
> excludefirstlast = FALSE,
>              includenightcrit = 1,
>              def.noc.sleep = c(1),
>              loglocation= c(),
>              outliers.only = FALSE,
>              criterror = 4,
>              relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
>              sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
>              colid=1,
>              coln1=2,
>              do.visual = TRUE,
>              nnights = 9,
>
>
> Thank you very much!
>

Cathy

messages.subject: non-wear detection vs. sleep/rest classification
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent!
Dear group members!

We have serious troubles when classyfing non-wear periods. Non-wear periods of up to 3 hours are often classyfied as rest/sleep periods via the angle algorithm. Interestingly, these periods are not detected and reported either in part2 (no angle alg. applied so far) nor part5.
I know that this can happen when the non-wear periods are very short but it also happens for periods of 2 hours (see example attached). We used both 60min and 30min windows for the non-wear detection, but the results were quite similar.

We also thought that this misclassification will also incorrectly lower the mean enmo values reported in part2 and part5 (since rest periods would be included in the calculation, whereas non-wear periods not (or maybe we misunderstood this)).

Did you ever experience the same problem and found a solution for it?

Many thanks!
Matteo

messages.subject: Re: non-wear detection vs. sleep/rest classification
messages.body_plain:
Hi Matteo,

I've had a similar problem, although in a slightly different context. I do a lot of sleep research with athletes, and one of the characteristics they have is taking the device off very soon after waking up (before a training session), which GGIR tends to classify as a 'continuation' of the sleep period, rather than as non-wear. I also tried fiddling around with the non-wear windows to try and dial up the sensitivity, but ~1 hour non-wear periods were still be mis-classified as sleep. In the end we've addressing the problem with a sleep log, but I'd be interested if anyone has any better ideas (sleep diary completion seems to be particularity spotty with athletes for some reason!).

I'm a relative GGIR novice, so I can't offer any solutions I'm afraid.

ATB

Andy
